name: Morocco
seoTitle: History of Morocco: Kingdom of the Maghreb, Green Pentagram Flag, and 1956 Independence
metaDescription: Explore the detailed history of Morocco. Discover the Alaouite Dynasty, Atlas Mountains, King Mohammed V, the green star flag, and solar energy.
mapFormation:
Spanning 446,550 square kilometers in Northwest Africa at the gateway between the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea across the Strait of Gibraltar, the Kingdom of Morocco (Al-Mamlaka al-Maghribiyya - 'The Western Kingdom') is framed by the snow-crested spine of the Atlas Mountains (Mount Toubkal, 4,167 meters) and the vast sands of the Sahara Desert.

Indigenous Amazigh (Berber) kingdoms traded across the Mediterranean during antiquity. In 789 CE, Idris I founded the Idrisid Dynasty and established the imperial city of Fes, the oldest continuous royal capital in Morocco. Successive Amazigh dynasties—the Almoravids and Almohads (11th–13th century)—ruled vast empires spanning North Africa and Muslim Andalusia (southern Spain).

Since 1666, Morocco has been governed by the Alaouite Dynasty. Following the Treaty of Fes (1912) establishing French and Spanish protectorates, King Mohammed V led the national liberation movement, securing sovereign independence on March 2, 1956.
flagHistory:
The national flag of Morocco—the Liwaa al-Maghrib—features a vivid crimson-red field bearing at the exact center a bold green five-pointed interlaced pentagram, officially codified by Royal Dahir of Sultan Moulay Youssef on November 17, 1915.

The historic red field has represented the Alaouite Dynasty and sovereign authority since the 17th century. The central Green Pentagram (Seal of Solomon / Khātim Sulaymān) was added to distinguish Moroccan maritime vessels from other red flags at sea. In Islamic and national symbolism: Red honors the courage, hardiness, and bravery of the Moroccan people; Green is the sacred color of Islam representing prosperity and peace; and the Five Points of the star symbolize the Five Pillars of Islam (Faith, Prayer, Charity, Fasting, and Pilgrimage).
freedomStory:
Morocco's struggle for independence was a courageous national mobilization spearheaded by the historic alliance between the Royal Monarchy and the nationalist resistance.

On January 11, 1944, nationalist leaders presented the historic Manifesto of Independence (Wathīqat al-Istiqlāl) demanding full sovereignty. In August 1953, French colonial authorities exiled Sultan Mohammed V to Corsica and Madagascar, igniting mass armed resistance (the Revolution of the King and the People / Thawrat al-Malik wa ash-Sha'b).

Sultan Mohammed V returned in triumph to Rabat on November 16, 1955, declaring the dawn of freedom. Independence was officially proclaimed on March 2, 1956. In November 1975, King Hassan II led the peaceful Green March of 350,000 unarmed citizens into the Sahara.
challenges: As a premier industrial and renewable energy hub in Africa hosting the world's largest concentrated solar farm (Noor Ouarzazate) and the high-speed Al Boraq bullet train, Morocco balances rapid modernization with climate adaptation. Foremost priorities include constructing major coastal seawater desalination plants to combat persistent drought, upgrading automotive and aerospace manufacturing, and hosting the 2030 FIFA World Cup.

faqs.question: What is the green star on the Moroccan flag?
faqs.answer: The green five-pointed star is the Seal of Solomon (Khātim Sulaymān), symbolizing health, wisdom, and the Five Pillars of Islam on the traditional red Alaouite field.

faqs.question: What was the Green March of 1975?
faqs.answer: The Green March was a peaceful mass demonstration in November 1975 organized by King Hassan II, in which 350,000 unarmed Moroccan citizens marched into the Western Sahara.

timeline.event: Idris I establishes the Idrisid Dynasty and founds the imperial city of Fes.
The Alaouite Dynasty assumes rule over Morocco, continuing to the present day.
The Treaty of Fes establishes French and Spanish protectorates over Morocco.
Morocco regains sovereign independence on March 2 under King Mohammed V.
King Hassan II leads the historic Green March of 350,000 citizens into the Sahara.
Inauguration of Al Boraq, the first high-speed rail line on the African continent.
